abstract: Noninvasive imaging of hemodynamics in deep cerebral arteries is essential for understanding cerebrovascular regulation, yet remains technically challenging. Existing angiographic techniques provide structural information with limited hemodynamic characterization, whereas transcranial ultrasound is limited by skull-induced attenuation, sensitivity and restricted deep-brain coverage. We introduce four-dimensional ultrasound cerebral angiography, a noninvasive approach using MBs, for in vivo visualization and quantitative assessment of cerebral arterial hemodynamics through the intact skull. We demonstrate imaging of the circle of Willis up to 7 cm deep in nonhuman primates, with quantification of large and small vessels, over 2.5 × 3.5 × 4 cm3 volumes, at 279-Hz volumetric rate for microbubble tracking and 151-µm spatial resolution after 3-min acquisition. This approach reveals flow organization, redistribution dynamics and interindividual variability, establishing four-dimensional ultrasound cerebral angiography as a methodological framework for deep, quantitative transcranial cerebrovascular imaging and provides a foundation for future translational development.
